threads.body: [General] Splitting on spaces can expose part of a sensitive value. `sun.java.command` does not preserve argument boundaries, so a launch argument such as `-DappSecret="abc def" --other=test` may appear here as `-DappSecret=abc def --other=test`; this code emits `-DappSecret=*** def --other=test`. Please redact continuations conservatively (for example, until a recognizable next option) rather than treating every space as a trustworthy boundary.

replies.body: Good catch. `sun.java.command` has already lost the argument boundaries, so even a recognizable next option could be part of the sensitive value. I updated this to conservatively redact everything after the sensitive property assignment and added an embedded-space regression case.

threads.body: [General] The trailing `.*` does not match line terminators unless DOTALL is enabled. Unix arguments can contain newlines, so a value such as `-DappSecret=abc\ndef` would become `-DappSecret=***\ndef`, exposing the remainder even though argument boundaries are unavailable. Enable DOTALL and add a multiline regression case so the full remainder is consumed.

replies.body:
Addressed in 181af00b819f5f820cc38d5253a8791c44918919.

Analysis: The flattened sun.java.command value has no recoverable argument boundaries, so once a sensitive property is found the redaction must consume line terminators as well as ordinary characters. Enabling DOTALL closes the newline leak, and the regression input proves that text after a newline is removed.

Upsides: Prevents partial disclosure of multiline secret values and later flattened command-line content.

Downsides: After a sensitive property is encountered, all remaining command-line text is redacted even when a newline was originally part of an argument.

threads.body: Surely someone is using `-D"my secret"=x`. Imo this is fine, but I guess we could also do a substring search for password and secret and remove everything that comes after.
